taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-01, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1056.4 | 23.97 | 23.97
2 | 1090.4 | 1.46 | 25.43
3 | 2606.8 | 3.17 | 28.60
4 | 3560.6 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-01, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-01 (Survey Area T)**

Station T-01 exhibits a 4-layer geoelectric section characterized by monotonically increasing resistivities with depth:
- **Layer 1:** 1056.4 $\Omega\cdot$m (0–23.97 m)
- **Layer 2:** 1090.4 $\Omega\cdot$m (23.97–25.43 m)
- **Layer 3:** 2606.8 $\Omega\cdot$m (25.43–28.60 m)
- **Layer 4:** 3560.6 $\Omega\cdot$m (basement/underlying formation)

**Curve Type Evaluation:**
The resistivity sequence satisfies $r_1 < r_2 < r_3$ (A) and $r_2 < r_3 < r_4$ (A), establishing an **AA-type** (or A-type) sounding curve. 

**Discrepancy Note:** The survey record on file incorrectly classifies this sounding as an **HA-type** curve. Because resistivity increases continuously from Layer 1 through Layer 4 with no conductive trough ($r_1 < r_2$), the archived HA classification does not fit the interpreted layer values.

{"curve_type_stated": "HA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
